title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: Morning Group Meditation
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Global Improvisation Initiative Symposium 2026
location: Lincoln Hall,1620 Southwest Park Avenue, Portland, OR 97201, USA
description:
This four day event includes curated panels, presentations and workshops and evening performances on the topic of improvisation. Whether you are new to and curious about improv, or a veteran, you are welcome to be part of this fun, inspiring and growth oriented event!

The Global Improvisation Initiative (GII) was launched to ignite a worldwide exploration of the art and impact of improvisation - deeply and collectively. Rooted in a profound appreciation for the rich history and diversity of the field, the GII seeks to unlock the infinite possibilities that lie ahead.

The GII Symposium 2026 will continue and deepen the explorations begun at previous symposiums (2017 in Southern California, 2019 in London, online in 2021, and exploration in 2023) with a specific focus on the central theme “Activate the Possible.”

In this moment of global conflict and uncertainty, the GII Symposium 2026 aims to serve as a vibrant intellectual and artistic hub for sharing, generating, and documenting new knowledge about improvisational theatre practices across the performing arts and beyond.

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Adult Book Discussion: The Lion Women of Tehran by Marjan Kamali
location: Sherwood Public Library, Community Room
description:
Read. Be inspired. Discuss.
We're hosting a book discussion in person at the library. If you love to talk about the books you've read, join us for a lively discussion of
The Lion Women of Tehran by Marjan Kamali
, which may be available as an e-book and audiobook in Libby as well as physical library copies which can be checked out. The first 10 people to register for this program can be given copies of the book provided generously by Friends of Sherwood Public Library.
Registration online is encouraged but not required.
From the publisher:
In 1950s Tehran, seven-year-old Ellie lives in grand comfort until the untimely death of her father, forcing Ellie and her mother to move to a tiny home downtown. Lonely and bearing the brunt of her mother's endless grievances, Ellie dreams of a friend to alleviate her isolation. Luckily, on the first day of school, she meets Homa, a kind, passionate girl with a brave and irrepressible spirit. Together, the two girls play games, learn to cook in the stone kitchen of Homa's warm home, wander through the colorful stalls of the Grand Bazaar, and share their ambitions for becoming "lion women." But their happiness is disrupted when Ellie and her mother are afforded the opportunity to return to their previous bourgeois life. Now a popular student at the best girls' high school in Iran, Ellie's memories of Homa begin to fade. Years later, however, her sudden reappearance in Ellie's privileged world alters the course of both of their lives. Together, the two young women come of age and pursue their own goals for meaningful futures. But as the political turmoil in Iran builds to a breaking point, one earth-shattering betrayal will have enormous consequences.

title: Cultivating Spaciousness and Abundance: Courage to Lead® for Sustainable Growth (Online)
location: Online
description: As leaders we are often called to come from a place of perpetual productivity, bottomless capacity, always giving and always "on". Yet the wholeness of who we are requires periods of reflection, receiving and renewal. When we do not honor this necessary balance, the wisdom of our hearts is harder to hear.What's growing in your life? What needs to be nourished for further growth? What do you want to prune or clear out?How do we listen to and honor what we need to be whole and in balance amid the demands and desires of an abundant life, in a way that allows for spaciousness, authenticity and joy?How do we tend to the garden of our lives and our work so that we can receive what we need to flourish?  Held during a time of peak growth and seasonal abundance, this Courage to Lead® two-day workshop invites us into spacious time for reflection, connection, and inner growth.Together we will…      Pause and cultivate our capacity to be present          Meaningfully engage with ourselves, others and nature with spaciousness and care          Take stock of our relationship to abundance and consider intentional paths of growth and clearing          Develop skills for holding meaningful conversations and building relational trust          Explore reflective and creative practices including the SoulCollage (https://soulcollage.com/about/)® method, an expressive arts practice used as a tool for accessing personal and archetypal wisdom      To ensure your SoulCollage (https://soulcollage.com/about/)® materials packet arrives before the workshop, register by June 24.Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Thursday-Friday, July 9-10, 2026, 9:30 a.m.-2:30 p.m. PT, OnlineFacilitators: Matsya Siosal, and Rafaela Steen, LCSWRegistration: $225. Includes 9 PDUs or CEUs, and materials packetRegister Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735427?epid=a1aUY000002Wikj)Scholarship Fund: We strive to keep our Courage retreats accessible to all who wish to participate. Please consider making a tax-deductible donation (https://engage.lclark.edu/register/gsecgiving?sys:gift:fund=4dfb9f4e-7351-4d84-91fe-531631c248c7&sys:gift:notes=Courage%20and%20Renewal%20Retreats%20Scholarship%20Fund) to our scholarship fund.Accessibility: We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. When registering, please let us know your access needs. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the Facilitators Matsya Siosal has developed her skills in leadership and facilitation for over 25 years, including roles with small and large for-profit corporations, mission-driven consumer goods companies, higher education, and as a consultant and entrepreneur. She has served as the director of the Center for Community Engagement at Lewis & Clark since 2015, after joining the department in 2010 to work in marketing and program management. Matsya is also co-founder and managing partner of Sea-O-Salt Bath Company (http://www.seaosalt.com/). Matsya is an experienced certified facilitator of Courage & Renewal programs. She has facilitated Circle of Trust, Courage to Lead, and Leading Together workshops and retreats since 2019, and is trained as a SoulCollage® (https://soulcollage.com/) facilitator. As a facilitator and coach, Matsya supports mission-driven leaders in accessing their authentic voice, and finding clarity and self-trust so they can show up with wholeheartedness and sustainability in their lives and work. Rafaela Steen, LCSW has been bringing people together for purpose, support, and connection for most of her adult life. For the last two decades, Rafaela has worked as an educational leader and strengths-based licensed clinical social worker offering consultation, guidance, and professional development related to mental health and well-being in K-12 schools and districts. Rafaela is an experienced facilitator, thought partner, convener, and problem solver who sees the importance of meaningful connection and joy within communities. Rafaela intentionally and strategically creates proactive, welcoming communities of care throughout her life, both personally and professionally.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. For the latest on professional development related to your specific interests, sign up for our mailing list! (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735441)

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Understanding, Exploring, and Supporting Perimenopause and Menopause Experiences in the Therapy Room (In-Person)
location: York 107, Lewis & Clark Graduate School, 615 S Palatine Hill Rd, Portland, OR
description: Menopause and perimenopause can magnify emotional and psychological distress—often showing up as irritability, mood shifts, anxiety, depression, grief, self-doubt, brain fog, and heightened emotional insecurity. These experiences can disrupt relationships, work functioning, and a client's sense of identity and self-efficacy. Many clients report little preparation, limited validation, and inconsistent guidance on what to expect or how to cope.  This skills-based in-person training equips clinicians and helping professionals with practical, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive tools to support clients who are navigating menopause-related mental health and life-transition stress.  Presenter Audrianna J. Gurr, LPC, CADCI, mental health clinician and author of I'm Still Hot! Surviving and Thriving in Your Mental Health During Menopause, will guide participants through a framework for identifying common emotional patterns, normalizing the experience without minimizing it, and selecting concrete interventions that can be used immediately in session.Following this training, participants will have the ability to:      Identify common emotional and psychological experiences that may intensify during perimenopause/menopause and differentiate them from other clinical presentations          Apply a brief session-ready framework for validating menopause-related distress while supporting client agency and self-compassion          Use the "Three Tiers" expectations tool to reduce anxiety-driven over-control and support realistic planning.           Teach assertiveness and boundary-setting skills using a "Personal Bill of Rights" lens to strengthen self-advocacy and relational functioning.          Adapt interventions with attention to equity and diversity, including how gender socialization, culture, and systemic barriers shape help-seeking, access to care, and empowerment during midlife transitions.    Details & RegistrationDate and Time: Friday, July 10, 2026, 9 a.m.-12 p.m.Location: York 107, Lewis & Clark Graduate School, 615 S. Palatine Hill Rd, Portland, ORPresenter: Audrianna J. Gurr, LPC, CADCI, MA, MS, is a Licensed Professional Counselor in Portland, Oregon, with nearly two decades of experience in community mental health and private practice. She has provided 15,000+ therapy sessions and integrates CBT, DBT, and other evidence-based approaches. title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.

"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Body Politics (Online)
location: Online
description: As clinicians, we need to be prepared to help clients deconstruct how their bodies have been storied.  This includes raising awareness of, and challenging, the impact of societal and relational power dynamics. These dynamics impact not only our inner dialog, but the everyday realities of our lives.  This course explores how we evaluate our bodies through the lens of "unidentified others," as well as the lived experience and consequences of looks, privilege and discrimination.  Participants will consider liberation-based counseling practices to counter the objectification, commodification, power and gendering of bodies in late capitalist societies.  The focus of this course is to raise awareness of body politics in the clinical practice and creating opportunities for change through individual and relational wellbeing.  This course is part of our Eating Disorders Certificate Program (https://graduate.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/).Course Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Saturday & Sunday, July 11 & 12, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Krystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHCCurrent Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 837-2, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education credit, $385. Individual Class: We welcome students seeking to take individual courses within the certificate program. Admission to the program is required. Click here for more information (https://www.lclark.edu/offices/admissions/certificate_programs/eating-disorders-cert/)Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735425)We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. If you have a disability that may impact your academic performance, you may request accommodations by meeting with the Office of Student Accessibility staff and submitting documentation on the Office of Student Accessibility website (https://www.lclark.edu/offices/student-accessibility/). Please be aware that the process for evaluation and implementation of accommodations could take 2-3 weeks, so please be in touch with the OSA as soon as possible. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the Instructor Krystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHC is a Licensed Professional Counselor and Clinical Supervisor, having earned her Masters Degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College in 2018. Drawing from an integrative feminist approach, her work is grounded in person-centered values, emphasizing authentic connection, and collaborative engagement. Her primary clinical focus is supporting clients in navigating identity development, body politics, neurodivergence, emotional codependency, highly sensitive personalities and other complex emotional experiences.  In addition to clinical work, Krystal is also passionate in training and mentoring emerging counselors. She is an adjunct professor, teaching a wide variety of graduate counseling courses with an underlying emphasis on counselor identity development, reflective practice, and cultivating professional resilience.  In both the classroom, and her clinical work, Krystal is committed to creating affirming spaces that honor intersectional identities and lived experience.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. For the latest on professional development related to your specific interests, sign up for our mailing list! (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735441)

About the Market
Our year‑round Farmers Market celebrates the best of our region – featuring local growers, farmers, ranchers, bakers, food producers, wineries, distilleries, cideries, and artisans
Click here for our interactive vendor map.

Summer Market Schedule (2026)
The Summer Market runs Saturdays, 9:00am–1:00pm, from May 2nd through October 31st. We operate outdoors, rain or shine, with ample parking and full ADA access.

Market Programming
We’re proud to offer a variety of free, family‑friendly programs throughout the season:
Power of Produce (POP) Club

A nationally recognized kids’ program offering weekly activities and tokens to purchase fresh produce and veggie plant starts for children ages 5–12. POP empowers kids to make healthy food choices, learn where their food comes from, and engage in hands‑on food and garden activities all summer long. Learn more.
Field‑to‑Fork Market Kitchen
Join us for cooking samples featuring seasonal produce from our vendors. Learn simple, budget‑friendly recipes and pick up tips for making the most of your market haul. Learn more.
Live Music
Enjoy local musicians every Saturday, adding a lively soundtrack to your market morning and creating a welcoming community atmosphere.
OSU Extension Master Gardeners
Visit the Master Gardener booth for expert advice on plant care, pest management, soil health, and home gardening. They’re here to help you grow with confidence.

SNAP & Double Up Food Bucks
We proudly accept SNAP/EBT, with up to a $20 Double Up Food Bucks match per market visit—made possible through grant support from Farmers Market Fund. Learn more.

Weather & Updates
The market runs rain or shine, but may close early or cancel in cases of severe weather. Visit our website for the latest updates, attending vendors, and event information.
Want weekly updates? Subscribe to our mailing list to stay connected with market news, events, and vendor highlights.

description:

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

6:15 - doors are open

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

title: Streetlight Manifesto
description:
Of all the various compliments Streetlight Manifesto have received from fans over the years, there is one in particular that seems to resonate most with the members of the band. After a show, a kid in torn jeans and a Pantera shirt, sporting ridiculous facial hair, will find one of the Streetlighters outside of the club and say hello, followed by “Man, I don’t listen to this kind of music, in fact I hate most ska bands, but you guys are something else.” Or it will be a jazz fan, sitting in the back of the venue during the set, bobbing his head, eyes closed while the band does their thing on stage. Or one of the club’s stagehands will comment, while helping break down the lighting rig, that he actually enjoyed a band he was working for for once, despite having heard thousands of bands on the job over the years. And therein lies Streetlight Manifesto’s appeal.
Seven guys, seven different musical backgrounds, seven different personalities, one band, one unique and unmistakable voice. Formed four years ago in New Jersey as an ad hoc group intended to put out one album and disappear, one thing lead to another and within a few months of their debut release, Everything Goes Numb, Streetlight Manifesto were officially a full time touring band, traveling the world, spreading their infectious and energetic tunes to all who would listen. One part rock, one part ska, with influences from latin, klezmer, folk, world, funk, jazz and classical thrown in, the band redefined what most people expected from a “ska” band. Three albums later, and after countless worldwide tours, the guys are still at it, still performing live to sold out shows filled with sweat drenched fans, all dancing and singing along at the top of their lungs. And the Streetlight boys wouldn’t have it any other way.

title: Chamber Music Northwest presents NEW@NIGHT: Across the Americas
description:
Some of the most innovative and revolutionary composers of our time embrace and elevate our “Songs from Home” theme that connects classical music with their own national heritage.

We’ll explore these sounds through Ligeti’s combination of Hungarian folk elements with modernism, as well as Wu Man’s Glimpses of Muqam Chebiyat highlighting traditions of Uyghur Muqam from China’s Xinjiang region. We will also experience works by two composers who will be with us—Portland’s own Kirsten Volness’s Shima Enaga, written for Portland pianist Yoko Greeney and connected to her Japanese heritage, and Kit Armstrong performing his own Études de dessin, inspired by Chinese ink painting and calligraphy. Our journey culminates with Armstrong performing Ligeti’s seventh Musica Ricercata on The Old Church’s incredible pipe organ.

Come join our artists for lively conversation about these exciting contemporary works both before and after their performances.

Sponsored by Alliance Bernstein.

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

******************************************************************

Purchase a 10 class package and save!
(packages must be purchased on site)

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

location: Online
description: This course will cover the topic of disordered eating and eating disorders in children.  Family therapy treatment strategies including the Maudsley method and other approaches will be discussed.  Additional focus will be placed on ways to foster healthy eating and positive lifestyle choices in families.  This course is part of our Eating Disorder Certificate Program (https://www.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/).Course Details & RegistrationDates: Friday & Saturday, July 18-19, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Dianne Lamberty Rogers, LMFT, CADCCurrent Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 878-22, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education credit, $385. If you have a disability that may impact your academic performance, you may request accommodations by meeting with the Office of Student Accessibility staff and submitting documentation on the Office of Student Accessibility website (https://www.lclark.edu/offices/student-accessibility/). Please be aware that the process for evaluation and implementation of accommodations could take 2-3 weeks, so please be in touch with the OSA as soon as possible. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the Instructor  Dianne Lamberty Rogers, LMFT, CADC has been a therapist serving kids, families and adults since completing her Masters in Marriage Couple and Family Therapy at Lewis and Clark Graduate School in 2015. Dianne has specialized in working with disordered eating and body image issues, families of clients with eating disorders, and Spanish speaking families.  Dianne has worked with youth and families in school based, intensive in-home, and outpatient settings providing drug, alcohol, and mental health treatment, and also in intensive outpatient and partial hospitalization settings for eating disorders. Dianne's work has included working with incarcerated youth, DHS-involved families, and foster and adopted youth.  Dianne conducts all of her work using a trauma informed and culturally competent lens as well as a body liberation standpoint. Dianne teaches the Family Therapy in the Treatment of Eating Disorders course in the Eating Disorders Certificate Program at Lewis & Clark Graduate School. She is also a Clinical Supervisor to Lewis and Clark and other graduate interns at Youth Contact Inc.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. description:
The Farmers Market Has Moved!
We’re now located at Clackamas Community College in Oregon City. Find us in Green Lot #1, near the corner of S Beavercreek Road and Clairmont Drive.
Click here to learn more about the new location.

About the Market
Our year‑round Farmers Market celebrates the best of our region – featuring local growers, farmers, ranchers, bakers, food producers, wineries, distilleries, cideries, and artisans
Click here for our interactive vendor map.

Summer Market Schedule (2026)
The Summer Market runs Saturdays, 9:00am–1:00pm, from May 2nd through October 31st. We operate outdoors, rain or shine, with ample parking and full ADA access.

Market Programming
We’re proud to offer a variety of free, family‑friendly programs throughout the season:
Power of Produce (POP) Club

A nationally recognized kids’ program offering weekly activities and tokens to purchase fresh produce and veggie plant starts for children ages 5–12. POP empowers kids to make healthy food choices, learn where their food comes from, and engage in hands‑on food and garden activities all summer long. Learn more.
Field‑to‑Fork Market Kitchen
Join us for cooking samples featuring seasonal produce from our vendors. Learn simple, budget‑friendly recipes and pick up tips for making the most of your market haul. Learn more.
Live Music
Enjoy local musicians every Saturday, adding a lively soundtrack to your market morning and creating a welcoming community atmosphere.
OSU Extension Master Gardeners
Visit the Master Gardener booth for expert advice on plant care, pest management, soil health, and home gardening. They’re here to help you grow with confidence.

SNAP & Double Up Food Bucks
We proudly accept SNAP/EBT, with up to a $20 Double Up Food Bucks match per market visit—made possible through grant support from Farmers Market Fund. Learn more.

Weather & Updates
The market runs rain or shine, but may close early or cancel in cases of severe weather. Visit our website for the latest updates, attending vendors, and event information.
Want weekly updates? Subscribe to our mailing list to stay connected with market news, events, and vendor highlights.

title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In

description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Dungeon Mastery 101

description:
This Summer level up your Dungeons & Dragons game by becoming a Dungeon Master! Every D&D game needs one player to take charge and create a world full of quests, monsters, treasure and adventure; maybe you’d like to BE that player… Learn the basics of D&D and how to run your own campaign for your friends with an experienced DM. We’ll discuss basic principles of running a game, how to run a session 0 to lay the groundwork, creating a party of adventurers, how to prep for a session- and what to do when your players run in a completely different direction than you expected!
No prior experience is needed- whether you’ve never played before and want to learn how to start your own game, or you’re a player who wants to try being a Dungeon Master, or even if you’ve done some DMing and just want to sharpen your skills with input from new players, all are welcome. This program will cover 5-6 sessions over the Summer (depending on the number of participants) to give everyone a chance to run an adventure for the others and experience Dungeon Mastery from behind the DM screen.

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Clinical Supervision (Online)

description: This online course is designed for current and future supervisors of graduate interns, clinical staff, and licensure candidates, and gives clinicians the information and skills necessary to develop competence in counseling supervision. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the InstructorJames Gurule, MA, LPC is a Licensed Professional Counselor with over four decades of clinical experience working in community mental health settings. In addition to clinical work as a Child and Family Therapist, James also provided clinical supervision with agency staff and was designated as an agency Lead Risk Manager at Lifeworks NW.  James also regularly provides professional trainings in ethics, solution focused clinical supervision and other strength-based supervisory practices through the Center for Community Engagement at Lewis & Clark Graduate School in Portland, Oregon. 6:15 - doors are open

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

******************************************************************

Purchase a 10 class package and save!
(packages must be purchased on site)

$15 per drop-in / 10 class package $135, get 1 class free/$13.50 per class) good for 1 year.

$10 Senior rate (10 class package $90, get 1 class free/ $9.00 per class) good for 1 year.

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

title: Supporting Ukrainians Through Trauma Informed, Culturally Competent Care (Online)
location: Online
description: This workshop invites clinicians into a deeper understanding of the historical and systemic forces shaping Ukrainian mental health. Participants will explore the lasting impacts of colonization, cultural erasure, forced assimilation, and ongoing geopolitical trauma, and how these experiences can show up in clinical settings.  Participants will gain insight into how these factors influence symptom presentation, help-seeking behaviors, and engagement in care, and how a fuller understanding of clients' lived experiences can support more accurate assessment and more effective, compassionate clinical work.  Together we will consider the roles of individual, intergenerational, and collective trauma, along with culturally relevant dynamics related to language, identity, and safety.  This workshop also provides a space to reflect on implicit bias, microaggressions, and cultural misunderstandings, and how they can impact treatment outcomes. Participants will develop strategies to address these dynamics and apply inclusive, equity-focused approaches in assessment and treatment planning.  Clinicians will leave the training equipped with practical tools to deliver ethical, effective, and culturally responsive mental health care for Ukrainian clients.Following this workshop, participants will have the ability to:      Describe historical and systemic factors, including cultural erasure, affecting Ukrainian mental health, and explain their impact on client care          Demonstrate trauma-informed and culturally competent interventions when working with Ukrainian clients through case examples          Identify instances of implicit bias and microaggressions in clinical scenarios and develop strategies to address them          Apply equity-focused approaches in treatment planning to ensure inclusive, ethical, and effective mental health care      This workshop may meet the OBLPCT Cultural Competence Continuing Education requirement. Click here for more information (http://www.oregon.gov/oblpct/Pages/CCCE.aspx)Details & RegistrationDate and Time: Tuesday, July 28, 2026, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m. PT, OnlineInstructors: Valentina Pishchanskaya-Cayanan, LMFT, CIMHP; and Yulia Brockdorf, RD, LD, CDCES, CST, NCC, LPC, BC-ADM, BC-TMH, LMHC, FAIHM, LN, CD, ACS, FAWMCost and Credits: $105, includes 4 CEUs. GSEC Alumni, Adjuncts, and Clinical Mental Health Supervisors save 20%. $50 student rate. Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/wf1W4MQ?epid=a1aUY000002XZAj)Accessibility: We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. When registering, please let us know your access needs. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the InstructorsValentina Pishchanskaya-Cayanan, LMFT, CIMHP is a Ukrainian licensed marriage and family therapist with extensive experience in clinical practice, higher education, and nonprofit leadership. She is the owner of Cayanan Counseling and Wellness, a virtual private practice serving clients across Oregon and Washington. Her practice is dedicated to providing compassionate, culturally attuned care with specializations in anxiety, trauma, and significant life adjustments. Valentina is EMDR-trained and integrates evidence-based, trauma-informed approaches to help clients navigate change, build resilience, and foster lasting well-being.  As a tenured faculty counselor at Clark College, Valentina provides psychotherapy, teaches, and develops programs to support diverse and underserved populations, including Ukrainian students. She is also the Co-Founder and Vice President of DAWN Inc., where she leads humanitarian and medical aid initiatives in Ukraine and supports refugee integration locally.  Valentina has presented at several conferences, including the Northwest Regional Equity Conference, on the needs of Ukrainians and the importance of culturally responsive, trauma-informed care. She has also spoken to policymakers, healthcare providers, and community leaders about the ongoing challenges faced by Ukrainians and ways to strengthen systems of support both locally and abroad. Through her clinical, educational, and nonprofit work, Valentina is recognized for advancing resilience, equity, and culturally informed trauma care in both local and international contexts.Yulia Brockdorf, RD, LD, CDCES, CST, NCC, LPC, BC-ADM, BC-TMH, LMHC, FAIHM, LN, CD, ACS, FAWM is a Ukrainian-American trauma psychotherapist and registered dietitian specializing in treating complex trauma and culturally competent care. She is the developer of the first combat psychotherapy model designed for delivery in active combat zones and has co-authored peer-reviewed publications on the psychological impact of drone warfare. Ms. Brockdorf provides direct psychotherapy to Ukrainian defenders along Ukraine's front lines and has trained mental health professionals, psychiatry residents, and healthcare providers on trauma-informed approaches and working with Ukrainian populations.  Ms. Brockdorf developed the trauma and mental health course module Connecting with Ukrainian Refugees: Meeting Their Needs with Better Care and Key Service for the Washington State Department of Health and has lectured at universities and medical schools on culturally responsive care for displaced populations. Her work has been published in peer-reviewed literature and she has been featured on Oregon's Think Out Loud and other media outlets. She previously served as Board President of the Oregon Board of Licensed Dietitians.  As president and co-founder of DAWN, Inc., Ms. Brockdorf has coordinated over $20 million in medical aid deliveries to Ukraine. She serves on the executive team of DefenseTech for Ukraine and advocates for U.S. support of Ukraine at state and federal levels, including meetings with NATO officials, representatives of the European Parliament, and members of the Government of Ukraine, and champions both local and international efforts in global security.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. title: AI In Education: Practical, Ethical, and Equitable AI Integration for Educators (Online)
location: Online
description: This hands-on workshop is designed for educators who want to confidently integrate AI into teaching, grading, and communication while maintaining academic integrity, equity, and human connection.  Participants will develop a practical understanding of how generative AI works, how to protect student privacy, and how to use AI as a productivity and thinking tool rather than a shortcut. Educators will practice prompt design, lesson planning, grading support, and student-facing AI literacy strategies that can be implemented immediately in their own courses.  Rather than focusing on tools alone, the workshop centers decision-making, ethics, and pedagogy so participants leave with confidence, clear boundaries, and ready-to-use instructional materials.  Following this workshop, participants will have an ability to:      Describe how generative AI functions at a practical level and identify key privacy and ethical considerations          Write effective prompts to support lesson planning, examples, and instructional materials          Use AI to design active learning activities and grading supports while maintaining instructor voice          Teach students how to use AI as a learning partner rather than a replacement for thinking    Respond to potential AI misuse using clear, restorative, and documented approaches  Details & RegistrationDate and Time: Wednesday, July 29, 2026, 9 a.m.-1 p.m, PT, OnlinePresenter: Jessica BernardsCost and Credits: $105, includes 4 PDUs. description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.

Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

title: Strengthening Support for LGBTQ+ Students in Challenging Times (Online)
location: Online
description: With changing and unstable politics, policies, and resources, knowing how to effectively support LGBTQ+ students has become increasingly complicated for educators and adults.  This workshop for school-based staff and administrators will ground into best practices in supporting LGBTQ+ students, and will explore practices that can help bring these guidelines into learning spaces.  This will include a review of Oregon's updated LGBTQ+ Student Success Plan (https://www.oregon.gov/ode/students-and-family/equity/lgbtq2siastudenteducation/pages/lgbtq2sia--student-success-plan.aspx), and time spent generating ideas for creative, innovative, and responsive implementation of the included tools and recommendations.  This workshop provides educators with an opportunity to connect with other supportive adults across the state and address the real impact that the complicated political climate has had on each of us as educators, community members, and supportive adults. Ultimately, this workshop will work to affirm educators as community change makers, and reinforce the concept of hope as an ongoing practice within our professions.Following the workshop, participants will be able to:Understand the use and modifications of Oregon's LGBTQ+ Student Success Plan  Name two tools or approaches that they can add to their practice as educators to increase student inclusion at their school or workplace  Identify personal practices of hope that support their professional practice as a trusted adult for LGBTQ+ students  Event Details & RegistrationDate and Time: Tuesday, August 4, 2026, 10 a.m-12 p.m., OnlineInstructor: Carson Varnum, MEdRegistration: $49, includes 2 PDUs. title: Treating The "What Ifs": Understanding & Applying Exposure & Response Prevention (ERP) [Online]
location: Online
description: What if I embarrass myself? What if I get sick? What if I sent the wrong person an email? What if I caused a car accident?  Anxiety is a natural, human response that no one is immune to experiencing. So when does anxiety turn from typical to disorder, and from adaptive into maladaptive?  On average, folks with OCD suffer 17 years before receiving correct diagnosis and effective treatment. It is vital for clinicians to become skilled at diagnosis and effective treatments such as Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) to ensure there is no delay in recovery.  For decades, ERP has been one of the most studied and effective therapies to treat anxiety disorders and OCD. When applied well, ERP can save lives, foster resilience, and lead to recovery. Many clinicians are unsure or even fearful of learning this modality because of misunderstanding the treatment model (example: that ERP is cruel, or further traumatizing).  ERP treatment targets reducing behaviors that get in the way of the life the person wants to live, increases tolerance of distressing feelings and empowers clients through self-efficacy.  This workshop provides an in-depth view of Exposure & Response Prevention, and modern perspectives on application. Following this training, participants will have a better ability to:      Better assess and differentiate diagnosis          Understand the principles of ERP          Identify response prevention techniques          Develop an exposure hierarchy in line with treatment protocols.
